lesson_title: Two Sizes of the Truth: Population and the Labour Market
hook_text: He applied for three years, then stopped. Officially? Not unemployed.
clip_script: Sort one family, seat by seat around the Sunday table, exactly as the survey-takers would. Grandpa Joseph, seventy: in the population, past working age. Little Neo, nine: too young. Ma, a nurse on night shift: on the team and on the field — employed. Uncle Vusi, four applications this month, checking the notice board every morning: on the team, sitting on the bench — officially unemployed. Ayanda in matric: full-time learner, off the sheet entirely. And cousin Sipho — three years of unanswered applications, until this winter he quietly stopped sending them. Here is the part that should make you sit up: the strict count strikes Sipho off the team sheet. Not unemployed, it says. The expanded count looks at him and says: he is plainly unemployed — count him. Thousands of real Siphos fill the gap between those two numbers, and Sipho never touches the strict unemployment rate — he vanishes into falling participation instead. So next time a jobless figure flashes on your screen, ask the economist's question: which count — and where did the Siphos go?
visual_style: A Sunday lunch table sorting into glowing rings — population, working-age, team sheet — with Vusi pulsing amber on a bench icon and Sipho dissolving off the sheet into a second ledger stamped 'expanded'; a stats board splitting into two columns of different heights.
pacing: Seat-by-seat sorting beat, dead stop on Sipho, quick-fire double question to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read every jobs headline like an economist.
